newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q2 1997 cocoa grind up 17.54 pct vs Q1 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q2 1997 cocoa grind up 17.54 pct vs Q1 1996.

text.p: U.S. cocoa grindings in the second quarter of 1997 rose 17.54 percent compared with the same year-ago period, to 97,223 tonnes, trading sources said on Friday.
The quantity of liquor melted rose by 28.77 percent versus second-quarter 1996 levels, to 1,629 tonnes, while the total butter melted increased by 6.61 percent to 15,093 tonnes.
The second quarter butter melted figure compared with a revised total of 14,157 tonnes in 1996, traders said.
Traders said the grind figures -- which represent the ammount of cocoa processed by U.S. manufacturers -- were higher-than-expected and should help bolster CSCE cocoa futures.

Most analysts had expected the U.S. second quarter grind to rise by 5 to 10 percent compared with the same period in 1996, although forecasts ranged widely from a 5 percent decrease to a 15 percent increase.
"It is a good number," said one trader. "It's better-than-expected."
